title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Galois theory of motives, arithmetic case over F̄_p. For q = p^n, M(q) is a multiplicative group of Frobenius eigenvalues attached to (pure) motives over F_q. These are the q-Weil numbers of integral weight w, i.e. |σλ| = q^{w/2} for every embedding σ, and units away from p, or perhaps only those that actually occur motivically. M^0(q) is the weight-0 part. The transition maps M(q) → M(q^m) are λ ↦ λ^m (Frobenius of F_{q^m} is the m-th power of Frobenius of F_q). The direct limit M(q^∞) splits as Z × M^0(q^∞), where Z records the weight.

The top-right formula says M^0(q^∞) = lim→ M^0(q^n) ≅ M^0 ⊗_Z Q. The limit kills the roots of unity, which are torsion, and the transition maps become isomorphisms after ⊗Q.

Over F̄_p he identifies M^0(p^∞) with P/U. Here P ⊂ Q̄* is the group of λ such that λ^n ∈ M^0(p) for some n, and U is the group of roots of unity. The map M^0(p^n) → P/U is λ ↦ λ^{1/n} mod U. The choice of root is irrelevant modulo U. It is compatible with the transition maps because (λ^m)^{1/(nm)} = λ^{1/n} mod U. Injectivity of the limit map holds because torsion dies in the limit.

Surjectivity is the question he then raises. Take λ' ∈ P with λ'^n = λ ∈ M^0(p). Choosing m = hn reduces the question to this: given λ ∈ M^0(p) and n ∈ N*, does there exist h ∈ N* with λ^h ∈ M^0(p^{hn})? Equivalently: is λ^h, already a Frobenius eigenvalue over F_{p^h}, also a Frobenius eigenvalue of some motive over F_{p^{hn}}?

If M^0(q) is defined as the abstract weight-0 Weil numbers, this is trivial: the weight-0 condition does not depend on q. If M^0(q) means eigenvalues actually realised by motives or abelian varieties, it is a genuine existence question. Honda–Tate (1966–68) answers it positively: every Weil q-number occurs.

The outcome is that the character group of the motivic Galois group over F̄_p (its weight-0 part) is P/U, the Weil-number group. Equivalently, the motivic Galois group is the 'Weil-number protorus' later written down by Saavedra, Langlands–Rapoport and Milne.

The lower half of the page is struck through with large diagonal strokes, so Grothendieck may have regarded this attempt as superseded. The reverse of the sheet shows an unrelated English typescript about ringed spaces.
errors: The phrase 'on constate que M^0(p^∞) s'identifie à ... P/U' needs care. One must quotient by the roots of unity, which are torsion and vanish in the direct limit. The identification with M^0 ⊗ Q requires surjectivity, and that is exactly the question left open (marked '??') at the bottom.

If M^0(q) is taken as abstract weight-0 Weil numbers, the final question is trivially yes. If it is motivic, it is non-trivial and needs Honda–Tate, which was not available in 1965. The page does not make the definition explicit.
The crossed-out claim that M^0(q')⊗Q → M^0(q)⊗Q is an isomorphism was abandoned on the page. Whether it holds is equivalent to the open surjectivity question.

ideas.what: Direct limit of Frobenius-eigenvalue groups over F_{p^n} along λ ↦ λ^m; splitting by weight Z × (weight 0)
ideas.modern_name: Weil-number group W(p^∞), character group of the Weil-number protorus P
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Langlands–Rapoport (1987), Milne ('Motives over finite fields', 1994)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; the motivic material reached print via Saavedra's thesis and Demazure/Kleiman expositions

ideas.what: Identification of the weight-0 limit with P/U via λ ↦ λ^{1/n} mod roots of unity
ideas.modern_name: W^0(p^∞) ≅ {λ ∈ Q̄*: λ^n weight-0 p-Weil number} / μ_∞; the kernel/central torus of the motivic Galois group over F̄_p

ideas.what: Question whether λ ∈ M^0(p) has a power λ^h lying in M^0(p^{hn}), i.e. realisability of Frobenius eigenvalues over larger fields
ideas.modern_name: Existence part of Honda–Tate theorem (every Weil q-number arises from an abelian variety)

missed.claim: Already in 1965 Grothendieck computes, at least conjecturally, the character group of the (weight-0 part of the) motivic Galois group over F̄_p as P/U, the group of Weil numbers modulo roots of unity. He also isolates exactly the realisability question that Honda–Tate later settled. This predates the standard attributions (Saavedra 1972, Langlands–Rapoport 1987, Milne 1994) of the Weil-number torus.
missed.quote: M^0(q=p^n) → P/U s'obtient par λ ↦ λ^{1/n} mod U ... la question devient si pour λ∈M^0(p), n∈N* étant donnés, il existe un h∈N* tel que λ^h ∈ M^0(p^{hn})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the Weil-number protorus as the motivic Galois group over F̄_p. It also shows Grothendieck framing the existence half of Honda–Tate as a Tannakian necessity before 1966.

deep.surprise_reason: It is an early, explicit form of the Weil-number group / motivic Galois torus over F̄_p, with the Honda–Tate-type question isolated. The underlying ideas are well known today and widely attributed to Grothendieck's circle via Saavedra, so this is a notable dated detail rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: Top-right: read 'M(q^∞) ≃ Z × M^0(q^∞), M^0(q^∞) = lim→ M^0(q^n) ≃ M^0 ⊗_Z Q'.
'λ ↦ λ^{1/n} mod U' is correct; 'la détermination de λ^{1/n} qu'on prend est sans importance' — the transcription has 'de U'.
'Ce lien' is probably 'Ceci car' / 'Cela a un sens car'.
The marginal hat-M(p) relates to 'M(p^n)^ ⊂ M̂(p)', likely denoting a saturation of M(p) in Q̄*.
'Trouver ...' is likely 'Transformation P/U ... ?' or 'Trouver directement P/U ?' — uncertain.
